title: Saving Hinton's job when the union tore up his Chicago card
summary: The Local 802 man rejects Hinton's card at the Cotton Club rehearsal; Thomas, knowing the rules, keeps him working two days a week until his six months were up.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Well, we found a thing in there that was great in that band. I mean...
It changed my whole life, Foots. I'll tell you.
And man, when you called me... After you got to New York, and you were talking about going back to Chicago, I said, "You've got to be crazy!"
Well, the union wouldn't let me stay. Cab...
But see, I knew that all you had to do was record and stick out them six months... And it's good that you played bass. I gave you one of your first bass jobs on a recording.
And then I knew that all you had to do was get your name around. Because there wasn't that many good bass players in New York!

But at the Cotton Club, on the day of the dress rehearsal, the union man came down to see the cards. And I had a Chicago card. And he tore it up and threw it on the floor. He told me, "Forget it." And Cab was learning

new lyrics. He sang all them new lyrics, "Copper Colored Gal Of Mine" and all these new lyrics. And they come and tell him, "Well, man, this bass player don't belong to the union." He didn't want to hear that. He could care less about the bass player. So he said, "Well, send him home. Tell him to go to the manager to get his ticket. Sorry, kid." He was trying to let me go.
I knew the law. And how I got involved in learning the law, I don't know. But I knew that you could play two days a week on a gig.
And you just couldn't take no steady job. You had to do that until your six months was up. And I knew that two days a week could hold you together...
And then I had them get a New York bass player and let him sub and do the best he can until, you know, you get your card.
I had been in the band almost six months on the road by the time I got there.
